decision: Adjudicated. One line of SysML 8.2.2.17.4 carries two defects, and the rule departs from the clause's literal text on both; each is recorded in deviations.json. First, the clause's second alternative ends in SendReceiverPart, which is defined nowhere in either specification, while SenderReceiverPart is defined two lines below in the same clause — a dangling reference repaired from the specification's own text (deviation SendReceiverPart-misspelling, follow_spec, SYSML21-408 open). Second, the clause writes ActionUsageDeclaration? where the Xtext and the clause's own three sibling declarations write ActionNodeUsageDeclaration?; those are different productions, the first carrying no 'action' keyword, and three files in the pinned corpus write exactly the keyword the literal reading would reject (deviation SendNode, follow_xtext, SYSML21-624 open). Not taken from the Xtext: its `( ActionBody | ( => ... ActionBody ) )` hoists the optional part into an explicit choice behind a '=>' syntactic predicate, an LL workaround for a parser generator this project does not use. The clause's `( ... )? ActionBody` says the same thing and is kept.
